# Commercial LLMs natively and with LangChain

## Chat models

A chat model is any class that implements LangChain's `BaseChatModel` interface. The provider SDKs in the optional notebook (and in [T2.2](/learn/ai-engineering-foundations/llm-provider-apis-and-model-selection/llm-provider-apis-and-model-selection-overview)) each return their own response object; the LangChain classes return the same one for every provider. Every chat model has the same three calls:

| Call | Takes | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `invoke` | a string, a message list or a `PromptValue` | one `AIMessage` |
| `batch` | a list of inputs | a list of `AIMessage`, run concurrently on a thread pool |
| `stream` | one input | the reply in chunks as it arrives |

The `AIMessage` carries more than the text. Lesson 2 of T4.1 reads three attributes:

- `.content`: the reply text.
- `.usage_metadata`: input, output and total token counts, under the same keys for every provider.
- `.response_metadata`: what the provider reported, such as `model_name` and `finish_reason`. On OpenAI a `finish_reason` of `length` means the reply hit the token limit and stopped mid-sentence, or mid-JSON; [lesson 6 of T4.1](/learn/langchain-and-langgraph-fundamentals/langchain-core-models-prompts-and-parsers/output-parsers#lesson-output-parsers) shows what the parsers make of that.

Changing provider changes one class. In the notebooks the same `prompt | model` chain runs on all of these:

| Class | Where the model runs | Model in the notebook |
|---|---|---|
| `ChatOpenAI` | OpenAI's API | `gpt-4o-mini` |
| `ChatGoogleGenerativeAI` | Google's Gemini API | `gemini-2.5-flash` |
| `ChatGroq` | Groq's hosted inference | `llama-3.1-8b-instant` |
| `ChatHuggingFace` over `HuggingFaceEndpoint` | Hugging Face Inference Providers | `moonshotai/kimi-k2-instruct-0905` |
| `ChatHuggingFace` over `HuggingFacePipeline` | your own machine | `TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0` |

The last three come from lesson 3 of T4.1's [Open Source LLMs with LangChain](https://github.com/Sourav692/rag-agents-engineering/blob/main/p03_llm_application_frameworks/m06_langchain_core/mandatory/notebook/03a_Open_Source_LLMs_with_LangChain.ipynb). `ChatHuggingFace` is a wrapper: the two Hugging Face classes underneath are completion-style LLMs, and the wrapper gives them the chat interface ([lesson 4 of T4.1](/learn/langchain-and-langgraph-fundamentals/langchain-core-models-prompts-and-parsers/inputs-and-outputs-messages-llm-vs-chat-model#lesson-llm-vs-chat-model)).

`init_chat_model` moves the choice out of the import line and into a string, which is how notebook 01b loads its model:

```python
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate

prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template("Explain {topic} in 2 bullet points")
llm = init_chat_model("openai:gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)
# llm = init_chat_model("groq:openai/gpt-oss-120b", temperature=0)

reply = (prompt | llm).invoke({"topic": "AI"})   # an AIMessage
```

The swap keeps the code running. It does not keep the replies the same: another model formats, refuses and rambles differently. For Larkspur, a provider change is a release like any other, checked against the golden questions from [T5.1](/learn/llm-and-retrieval/rag-from-first-principles/rag-from-first-principles-overview) before it ships.

## Key Takeaways

- Every LangChain chat model offers `invoke`, `batch` and `stream` and returns an `AIMessage`, with token counts under the same keys for every provider.
- Read `.response_metadata` as well as `.content`. A `finish_reason` of `length` means the reply hit the token limit and stopped mid-sentence or mid-JSON.
- Changing provider changes one class or one `init_chat_model` string, but the replies change too. Treat a provider swap as a release and check it against the golden questions.

## Check yourself

<details>
<summary>1. What does a LangChain chat model give you that calling each provider SDK directly does not?</summary>

The same response object for every provider. Each SDK returns its own object, while every `BaseChatModel` offers `invoke`, `batch` and `stream` and returns an `AIMessage`, with token counts under the same keys in `.usage_metadata`. Changing provider then changes one class.

</details>

<details>
<summary>2. A Larkspur reply on OpenAI stops mid-JSON, and its response metadata shows a finish reason of length. What happened?</summary>

The reply hit the token limit and stopped mid-sentence, or here mid-JSON. `.response_metadata` reports what the provider said, and `finish_reason` of `length` is OpenAI's signal for it. Lesson 6 of T4.1 shows what each output parser makes of such a truncated reply.

</details>

<details>
<summary>3. You change the init_chat_model string from an OpenAI model to a Groq model and the chain still runs. Can you ship the change?</summary>

Not yet. The swap keeps the code running, but another model formats, refuses and rambles differently, so the replies change. For Larkspur, a provider change is a release like any other, checked against the [T5.1](/learn/llm-and-retrieval/rag-from-first-principles/rag-from-first-principles-overview) golden questions before it ships.

</details>
